docs.title: Welcome to the Fashion MNIST Classifier Project Documentation!
docs.text: This documentation provides a comprehensive guide to the Fashion MNIST Classifier, a deep learning project built with PyTorch. This project showcases a complete machine learning pipeline, from data preparation and model development to training, evaluation, and experiment tracking.

docs.title: Project Goals
docs.text:
• To implement a modular deep learning pipeline for image classification.
  • To demonstrate best practices in MLOps, including configuration management, structured logging, and experiment tracking with MLflow.
  • To explore various Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) architectures, from simple baselines to more advanced designs like ResNet.
  • To provide a clear, reproducible, and well-documented example of a PyTorch project.

docs.title: Architecture
docs.text:
• Modular PyTorch implementation
  • Abstract base classes for extensibility
  • Type hints throughout codebase
  • Professional logging system

docs.title: Models Implemented
docs.text:
• VanillaCNN: Baseline 2-layer CNN
  • DeepCNN: Enhanced VanillaCNN with BatchNorm and Dropout
  • FashionResNet: ResNet-like architecture with residual connections

docs.title: MLOps Integration
docs.text:
• MLflow experiment tracking
  • Automated model logging and versioning
  • Performance metrics visualization
  • Hyperparameter tracking

docs.title: Quality Assurance
docs.text:
• Comprehensive unit tests
  • Automated CI/CD with GitHub Actions
  • Code linting with flake8
  • Type checking support

docs.title: What You'll Find Here
docs.text:
• Installation Guide: How to set up your development environment.
  • Usage Instructions: How to run the training, evaluation, and prediction scripts.
  • API Reference: Detailed documentation for the project's Python modules and functions.

Start by installing the project locally to get set up!

docs.title: Installation Guide
docs.text: This guide will walk you through setting up your development environment for the Fashion MNIST Classifier project.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
Before you begin, ensure you have the following installed:

  • Python 3.8 or higher
  • Git
  • pip (Python package installer)

docs.title: 1. Clone the Repository
docs.text:
Clone the project from GitHub:

git clone https://github.com/radixon/fashion-mnist-classifier.git
cd fashion-mnist-classifier

docs.title: 2. Create and Activate a Python Virtual Environment
docs.text:
It's highly recommended to use a Python virtual environment to manage project dependencies and avoid conflicts with other Python projects or your system-wide Python installation.

# Create the virtual environment
python3 -m venv .venv

# Activate the virtual environment
source .venv/bin/activate  # Linux
.venv\Scripts\activate  # Windows

docs.title: 3. Install Core Project Dependencies
docs.text:
Install the Python packages listed in requirements.txt.

# Upgrade pip
python3 -m pip install --upgrade pip

# Install project dependencies
pip install -r requirements.txt

# Install project in development mode
pip install -e .

docs.title: 4. Verify Installation
docs.text:
# Run all tests
pytest tests/ -v

docs.title: 4. Install PyTorch and TorchVision
docs.text:
PyTorch installation varies based on your operating system and GPU (CUDA) availability. You must install PyTorch and TorchVision separately using the command from their official website.

  1. Go to the official PyTorch website: https://pytorch.org/get-started/locally/
  2. Select your desired configuration.
  3. Copy the provided installation command and run it in your activated virtual environment.

docs.title: 6. Download Data
docs.text:
The Fashion MNIST dataset will be automatically downloded the first instance of running training.

python3 scripts/train.py

Once these steps are complete, your development environment is ready!

docs.title: Project Structure
docs.text:
# Project Structure

This project follows a professional and modular structure to ensure maintainability, scalability, and clear separation of concerns.

fashion-mnist-classifier/
├── .github/workflows/  # CI/CD and deployment workflows
├── app/                # Interactive applications 
├── configs/            # Configuration files 
├── data/               # Raw and processed data storage
├── docs/               # Project documentation source files
├── notebooks/          # Jupyter notebooks for exploration and analysis
├── results/            # Saved outputs 
├── scripts/            # Main executable scripts 
├── src/                # Core source code 
│ ├── data/             # Data loading and preprocessing modules
│ ├── evaluation/       # Evaluation logic and visualization
│ ├── models/           # Neural network architecture definitions
│ ├── training/         # Training loop and callback logic
│ └── utils/            # Utility functions 
├── tests/              # Unit and integration tests
├── .gitignore          # Specifies files/folders for Git to ignore
├── mkdocs.yml          # MkDocs configuration for documentation site
├── README.md           # High-level project overview
└── requirements.txt    # Project dependencies

docs.title: Usage Instructions
docs.text:
This section details how to use the various scripts and notebooks provided in this project.

Ensure you have completed the Installation Guide and your virtual environment is activated before proceeding.

docs.title: 1. Configuration
docs.text: All key parameters for data, training, model, and paths are managed in configs/config.yaml. Before running any training or evaluation, review this file to adjust settings as needed.

docs.title: 2. Running the Scripts
docs.text: All main scripts are located in the scripts/ directory and should be executed from the project's root directory.

docs.title: Train the Model
docs.text:
The train.py script orchestrates the model training process. It loads configurations, prepares data, initializes the chosen model, and runs the training loop. The 'train.py' script also logs experiment details to MLflow and saves the best model checkpoint.

python3 scripts/train.py
  • Output: Training progress will be displayed in the console and logged to a timestamped file in results/logs/. MLflow will record parameters, metrics, and artifacts in the mlruns/ directory. The best model will be saved to models/best_model.pth.

docs.title: Evaluate the Model
docs.text:
The evaluate.py script loads a trained model, evaluates its performance on the test set, and generates detailed reports and visualizations.

python3 scripts/evaluate.py
  • Output: Evaluation results will be displayed in the console and logged. Detailed metrics (JSON) and a confusion matrix plot will be saved to results/metrics/ and results/figures/ respectively.

docs.title: Make Predictions (Coming Soon)
docs.text:
The predict.py script will allow you to make predictions on new data using a saved model.

python3 scripts/predict.py --image_path path/to/your/image.png

docs.title: 3. Using Jupyter Notebooks
docs.text: Jupyter Notebooks are used for exploratory data analysis (EDA) and experimentation.

docs.title: Start JupyterLab
docs.text:
From the project's root directory, launch JupyterLab:

jupyter lab

This will open JupyterLab in your web browser. Navigate to the notebooks/ directory.

docs.title: Explore the Dataset (EDA)
docs.text:
Open 01_data_exploration.ipynb. Run all cells to:

  • Visualize sample Fashion MNIST images.
  • Analyze class distributions.
  • Understand the dataset's characteristics.

Plots generated during EDA will be saved to results/figures/.

docs.title: Baseline Model Experimentation
docs.text:
Open 02_baseline_models.ipynb. Run all cells to:

  • Train the VanillaCNN model interactively.
  • Observe training and validation loss/accuracy curves.
  • Generate and save plots of training history and confusion matrices.
  • Experiment with quick parameter changes.

docs.title: 4. MLflow UI
docs.text:
To view and compare your experiment runs, start the MLflow UI:

mlflow ui

Then, open your web browser and navigate to the address displayed in your terminal (usually http://localhost:5000).
